audits.title: AUDIT OF OXYGEN PRESCRIBING IN A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL.
audits.standard: Local guidelines: all patients receiving oxygen have a prescription with target saturations, device and nurse signature within 12 hrs; target 100%
audits.setting: All wards, children's hospital, Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
audits.intervention: New paediatric medication chart with oxygen section and training package.

cycle2.result: 4/18 (22%) had a prescription, all medical patients; target saturation 100%, device 25%, nurse signature 100%.

audits.other_findings: Critical care had not engaged with the new chart; numbers were small.
audits.citation: Wheeler L, James J, Byrne S, Forton J. AUDIT OF OXYGEN PRESCRIBING IN A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.36. PMID: 27540216.

audits.title: 170 A closed loop audit on oxygen prescription in the emergency department in Ipswich Hospital
audits.standard: BTS guidelines on emergency oxygen (2017): oxygen prescribed with target saturations

cycle1.result: 14% of patients had target oxygen saturations prescribed.

audits.intervention: Results and BTS recommendations presented in departmental teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: 20% had target oxygen saturations prescribed (p=0.595, not significant).

audits.other_findings: Teaching alone was insufficient; nursing prompts and senior spot checks were recommended.
audits.citation: Sudin E, Kathwadia D, Udofa E, Bose A. 170 A closed loop audit on oxygen prescription in the emergency department in Ipswich Hospital. Emergency Medicine Journal. 2020;37(12):846.1-846. doi:10.1136/emj-2020-rcemabstracts.41.

audits.title: An audit of the effect of oxygen prescription charts on clinical practice
audits.standard: Adequate oxygen prescription (device, flow rate or inspired oxygen concentration, and target saturation), administration and monitoring
audits.setting: Wellington Hospital, teaching and tertiary referral hospital
audits.intervention: New drug chart with a specific oxygen prescription section and targeted educational lectures mainly to medical staff.

cycle2.result: Oxygen prescribed in 39/98 (39.8%), RR 2.3 (95% CI 1.3 to 3.9); adequate prescription 36/98 (36.7%), RR 6.2 (95% CI 2.5 to 15.0).

audits.other_findings: No change in assessment of room-air saturations with oxygen started at 92% or below, or in titration of oxygen to saturations.
audits.citation: Wijesinghe M, Shirtcliffe P, Perrin K, Healy B, James K, Weatherall M, et al.. An audit of the effect of oxygen prescription charts on clinical practice. Postgraduate Medical Journal. 2010;86(1012):89-93. doi:10.1136/pgmj.2009.087528.

audits.title: Audit of oxygen administration to achieve a target oxygen saturation range in acutely unwell medical patients
audits.standard: Documented target SpO2 range and SpO2 kept within it
audits.setting: Wellington Regional Hospital; inpatients with pneumonia, heart failure, asthma or COPD

cycle1.result: Target SpO2 range documented in 62 of 100; mean (SD) proportion of SpO2 measurements within range 56.2 (30.6)%.

audits.other_findings: A hypercapnic target range was associated with SpO2 above range (OR 5.34).
audits.citation: Harper J, Kearns N, Bird G, McLachlan R, Eathorne A, Weatherall M, et al.. Audit of oxygen administration to achieve a target oxygen saturation range in acutely unwell medical patients. Postgraduate Medical Journal. 2021;98(1160):461-465. doi:10.1136/postgradmedj-2020-139511.

audits.title: An audit of oxygen prescribing in acute general medical wards.
audits.setting: Acute general medical wards, Sunderland Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: Less than a fifth of patients receiving oxygen had a prescription written in their medical notes.

audits.other_findings: Authors highlight possible legal implications and the need for nurse vigilance.
audits.citation: Howell M. An audit of oxygen prescribing in acute general medical wards. Prof Nurse. 2001;17(4):221-224. PMID: 12030174.

audits.title: The use of oxygen in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a prospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management.
audits.standard: National COPD guidelines: initial FiO2 no more than 0.28
audits.setting: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital; pre-hospital and hospital emergency care

cycle1.result: Oxygen with FiO2 above 0.28 was common and predominantly initiated in the ambulance (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Patient awareness, disease identification aids and ambulance protocols suggested for improvement.
audits.citation: Denniston AK, O'Brien C, Stableforth D. The use of oxygen in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a prospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management. Clin Med (Lond). 2002;2(5):449-451. doi:10.7861/clinmedicine.2-5-449. PMID: 12448594.

audits.title: An audit of oxygen therapy on a respiratory ward.
audits.standard: Oxygen should be prescribed like any other drug

cycle1.result: Only 5% of patients had an oxygen prescription; 14 issues with oxygen delivery.

audits.intervention: Education sessions on oxygen prescribing and oxygen therapy

cycle2.result: 20% had a prescription (P=0.042); oxygen delivery issues fell to one.

audits.other_findings: Prescribing rates remained unsatisfactory despite doctors being made aware of findings.
audits.citation: Hickey S. An audit of oxygen therapy on a respiratory ward. Br J Nurs. 2007;16(18):1132-1136. doi:10.12968/bjon.2007.16.18.27507. PMID: 18073684.

audits.title: Improved oxygen prescribing using a nurse-facilitated reminder.
audits.setting: 26-bed medical admissions unit in a 678-bed teaching hospital, Glenfield Hospital, Leicester

cycle1.result: Oxygen prescribed in 0%; appropriate oxygen therapy 70.6%; type 1 respiratory failure errors 18.4%; type 2 errors 61.3%.

audits.intervention: MAU nurse education and a nurse-facilitated oxygen prescribing reminder to junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Oxygen prescribed in 49% (p < 0.0001); appropriate therapy 76.5% (p = 0.65); type 1 errors 3.8% (p = 0.13); type 2 errors 44.0% (p = 0.49).

audits.citation: Medford A, Bowen J, Harvey J. Improved oxygen prescribing using a nurse-facilitated reminder. Br J Nurs. 2009;18(12):730-734. doi:10.12968/bjon.2009.18.12.42886. PMID: 19543159.

audits.title: Assessing the use of initial oxygen therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: a retrospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management.
audits.standard: Recommended controlled inspired oxygen (FiO2 ≤0.28) in COPD exacerbations
audits.setting: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sydney (pre-hospital and emergency department care)

cycle1.result: COPD recognised in 53%; SpO2 recorded in 124; FiO2 >0.28 given in 54 patients in ambulances and 35 in the ED.

audits.other_findings: 53 needed non-invasive ventilation (29 of whom had FiO2 >0.28 in ED); 7 admitted to ICU and 10 died.
audits.citation: Susanto C, Thomas PS. Assessing the use of initial oxygen therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: a retrospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management. Intern Med J. 2015;45(5):510-516. doi:10.1111/imj.12727. PMID: 25682723.

audits.title: Doctors learn new tricks, but do they remember them? Lack of effect of an educational intervention in improving Oxygen prescribing.
audits.setting: Inpatients, Canterbury District Health Board, Christchurch

cycle2.result: Oxygen prescription rate 13.9% four years on, a significant deterioration from 58.8% at the second audit (P = 0.01).

audits.other_findings: Second audit (102 inpatients, September 2009 to February 2010) showed improvement from 24.5% to 58.8% (P = 0.01), which was not sustained.
audits.citation: Myers H, Taylor J, Finn RS, Beckert L. Doctors learn new tricks, but do they remember them? Lack of effect of an educational intervention in improving Oxygen prescribing. Respirology. 2015;20(8):1229-1232. doi:10.1111/resp.12614. PMID: 26332938.

audits.title: Improving Compliance With Valid Oxygen Prescriptions for Surgical Inpatients in a District General Hospital: A Single-Centre Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society guideline: all inpatients should have a valid oxygen prescription with a target saturation range (target 100%)
audits.setting: Two general surgical wards, Royal Blackburn Teaching Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 18% had oxygen prescribed; 0% compliance among patients requiring oxygen.

audits.intervention: Reminders on handover sheets, visual prompts on the ward, announcements at nursing huddles and WhatsApp reminders to ward doctors.

cycle2.result: 54.8% had oxygen prescribed (χ²(1, N=64) = 9.3, p < 0.01); 90.9% compliance among patients requiring oxygen.

audits.other_findings: Compliance stayed below the 100% BTS target; authors suggest electronic prescription prompts.
audits.citation: Hussain S, Mobarak Z, Ahmad SY, Shoaib H, Arif A, Ahmed MA. Improving Compliance With Valid Oxygen Prescriptions for Surgical Inpatients in a District General Hospital: A Single-Centre Quality Improvement Study. Cureus. 2024;16(10):e71600. doi:10.7759/cureus.71600. PMID: 39552963.

audits.standard: British Thoracic Society guideline for oxygen prescription

audits.title: Oxygen on Arrival: An Audit of Prescription Practices in the Emergency Assessment Unit.
audits.standard: Guidelines on oxygen prescribing at admission clerking
audits.setting: Emergency Assessment Unit, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: 45% (45) prescribed oxygen at initial clerking and 26% (26) later; 29 (29%) never had a documented prescription; 8/19 (42%) COPD patients never prescribed oxygen.

audits.other_findings: Errors in 4 (9%) prescriptions; out-of-hours admissions had higher omission rates; 9/11 (82%) junior doctors lacked formal training.
audits.citation: Khalid F, ElTahir RM. Oxygen on Arrival: An Audit of Prescription Practices in the Emergency Assessment Unit. Cureus. 2025;17(8):e89283. doi:10.7759/cureus.89283. PMID: 40909075.

audits.title: Oxygen Stewardship in Adult Critical Care: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.setting: Mixed adult ICU, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital

cycle1.result: Median 63% (IQR 57-65) of patient-days outside target saturation ranges.

audits.intervention: Standardised oxygen weaning protocol, multidisciplinary education, audit and feedback via spot checks, workflow reminders and iterative refinement from staff surveys and interviews.

cycle2.result: Median 20% (IQR 15-22) of patient-days outside target ranges.

audits.other_findings: Oxygen consumption fell for conventional oxygen, NIV and mechanical ventilation, but high-flow nasal cannula stayed less compliant with no significant reduction.
audits.citation: Ong WJD, Li GJ, Azul LMA, Trajico AK, Tan WKR, D'Souza J, et al.. Oxygen Stewardship in Adult Critical Care: A Quality Improvement Initiative. Nurs Crit Care. 2026;31(3):e70476. doi:10.1111/nicc.70476. PMID: 41940418.
